key_insight: MatScope finds that strong calculations and physical explanations do not guarantee reliable predictions or comparisons between closely related material states.
engineering_relevance: AI-assisted materials workflows need condition-matched evidence and quantitative checks before model predictions guide experimental decisions.
method: M1 tests unaided, condition-specific reasoning on 200 tasks across ten research functions using aluminium and high-entropy alloys.
M2 tests agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions.
MatEvoBench-20 tests forecasts across scientific dependency chains and revisions as observations accumulate.
evidence_signal: Across eleven model deployments, calculations from supplied inputs and many physical explanations performed well, while fine-grained estimates, similar-state comparisons and quantitatively supported choices remained weaker.
watch_item: Related literature can mismatch experimental conditions or baselines, and new observations can destabilize previously accurate predictions.
paper_title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
